sentences.text: The petitioner is the sole accused in Crime No.1192/2023 of Paravoor Police station, Kollam district for offenses alleged under Section 376, 376(2)(n) and 506(i) of the Indian Penal Code.
As per Annexure-A1 order, the petitioner was granted regular bail.
One of the conditions for grant of bail was that, the petitioner shall surrender his passport before the jurisdictional Court, which condition was complied with.
3. The petitioner filed C.M.P.No.175/2024 seeking release of his passport, for the purpose of renewal of the same.
It is averred that, his passport expired on 24.02.2024, a copy of which is produced as Annexure-A3 herein.

The same was dismissed by the learned Magistrate vide Annexure- A2 order finding that, the final report has already been filed and that no direction has been issued by the High Court for release of passport, while granting bail.
4. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor, this Court is of the opinion that the instant Crl.M.C. is only to be allowed.
This Court notice that, investigation in the crime is over and final report has already been filed.
In view of the fact that the instant crime is of the year 2023, there is no immediate prospects for commencement of trial.

The petitioner wants his passport to be renewed, for which purpose he seeks return/release ..4..
of his passport, which was surrendered before the Court as part of the bail conditions.
This Court finds no legally recognizable reason to refuse such a relief sought for by the petitioner.

Even in respect of the matters where the accused persons seek permission of the Courts to travel abroad in connection with their job, the passports are liable to be released, as has been settled in Ashok Kumar v. State of Kerala [2009 2 KLT 712] and Muhammed v. State of Kerala [2012 4 KLT 655].

entities.text: Ashok Kumar v. State of Kerala [2009 2 KLT 712]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Muhammed v. State of Kerala [2012 4 KLT 655]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The legal position has been clarified by a learned Single Judge of this Court in Radha v. State of Kerala [Manu/KE/2454/2015].
5.

This court also takes into account the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the disputes between the petitioner and the defacto complainant have been amicably settled and Crl.M.C.No.3296/2024 is pending consideration to quash the very case itself.

In support of the same, the learned ..5..
counsel would hand over an affidavit sworn to by the defacto complainant, indicating that the disputes have been settled and that she is no more interested to prosecute the case as against the petitioner.
In these circumstances, Annexure-A2 order will stand set aside.
The learned Magistrate will pass orders permitting release of the petitioner's passport, with appropriate conditions after taking note of the binding precedents on the point.

Needless to say that the usual conditions with respect to execution of the bond and also an affidavit by the petitioner undertaking to appear before the court for the purpose of trial as and when required, etc., will be incorporated.
